english.html: need be, by natural death <sup class="mk" data-key="a">a</sup>: of which justice, because the hangmen are the executors, they are called in France Executors of high justice.

notes.gloss: Imperium aut merum aut mixtum est. Merum est imperium habere gladii potestatem ad animadvertendum facinorosos homines: power is either pure or mixed; pure power is to have the power of the sword to punish wicked men — the text Coras translates.

english.html: Before the house of the said Martin

It was also fitting that this abominable and prodigious impostor, the infamous minister of the ruin of the house of the said Martin, should be executed before that house where he had committed, and so long continued, his treachery <sup class="mk" data-key="a2">a2</sup>. Whereupon the words of Callistratus the Jurisconsult are worthy to be transcribed here. BRIGANDS and notorious thieves, says he, ought to be hanged in the place where they have practised their brigandage, so that the others, seeing them, may be turned away from like evil deeds, and the kinsfolk of the murdered and the injured may receive some relief and consolation, seeing justice justly rendered, and the penalty executed, in the place of the evil deed <sup class="mk" data-key="b">b</sup>.

notes.citation: Digest 48.19.28 (De poenis, l. Capitalium, Callistratus), § Famosos (D. 48.19.28.15); and the Authentica Qua in provincia inserted in Code 3.15 (Ubi de criminibus agi oportet), drawn from Novel 69
notes.original: l. capitaliũ. P. famoſos. D. de pœn. Aut. qua in prouin cia. C. vbi de crim. ag. op.
notes.gloss: The Authentica: in whatever province a man offends, there let him be punished — the rule that the penalty is executed where the crime was committed.

Famosos latrones in his locis, ubi grassati sunt, furca figendos compluribus placuit, ut et conspectu deterreantur alii ab isdem facinoribus et solacio sit cognatis et adfinibus interemptorum eodem loco poena reddita, in quo latrones homicidia fecissent — the passage Coras transcribes.

english.html: A penalty, assuredly, as has been shown above, worthy of so detestable a lecher and heinous traitor <sup class="mk" data-key="a3">a3</sup>. For hanging on the gibbet is, of all the punishments the ancients were able to devise, the most foul, ignominious, base and infamous: wherefore the Poets have called such a death base, filthy, ugly, unsightly and wretched. As Virgil, speaking of Amata, mother of Lavinia, who, indignant against her daughter, whom Aeneas had married (although she and King Latinus her father had pledged her to Turnus), hanged and strangled herself, saying <sup class="mk" data-key="b2">b2</sup>,

notes.citation: Accursius (Glossa ordinaria) on Digest 49.16.3 (De re militari, l. 3, Modestinus); Baldus on the fragment Cum quidam in the title De iureiurando (Digest 12.2, or Code 4.1 De rebus creditis et iureiurando) — fragment not identified
notes.original: Accurſe en la l. iij. D. de re mili. Baldé en la l. cũ qui dã. de iureiur.
notes.gloss: For the point "shown above", that hanging is the most infamous of deaths; the Gloss on D. 49.16.3, which lists the soldier's penalties, is where the glossators rank the furca.
Et nodum informis leti trabe nectit ab alta: Amata's suicide; the print's nondum is a slip for nodum.

english.html: And she knots from a high beam the noose of an unsightly death (Et nodum informis leti trabe nectit ab alta).
